items.desc_en:
Cisco Secure Email Gateway Arbitrary File Write Vulnerability

A vulnerability in the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system.

This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. Podman: The `podman run` command can be instructed to disable almost all sandboxing by image annotation
### Impact
Podman v4.4.0 added a feature where container checkpoints (from the `podman container checkpoint` command) could be distributed via OCI registry, and pulled from that registry and run via the `podman run` command. This allowed easy transfer of checkpoints between systems. However, checkpoints allow complete control of how the container is created - including full control of the container sandbox. Mercury: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in /api/terminals - access control bypass
### Summary
A missing comma in `mercury_app/block_handler.py`'s `BLOCKED_PATTERNS` list causes the blocklist to fail to cover the `/api/terminals` endpoint. As a result, any unauthenticated attacker can spawn a full, interactive OS-level shell on the host running Mercury.

items.desc_en: IBM DataStage on Cloud Pak for Data 5.4.0.0 allows an unauthenticated user to perform an arbitrary write into shared Redis under any tenant's key. This collapses the platform's credential-encryption boundary and lets an anonymous caller poison any tenant's cached flow parameters.
